question: A worker lifts a rice bag of 10 kg from the ground and puts it on the truck 2 m above the ground. Calculate the work done by him on the rice bag. (Given, g= 10 ms-2)
solution:
The correct answer is __**200 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To calculate the **work done**, we use the formula: **Work Done (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d)**.
 
• The **force** exerted by the worker is equal to the weight of the rice bag, which is calculated by: **Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• Here, the **mass** (m) of the rice bag is **10 kg**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** (g) is given as **10 ms⁻²**.
 
• So, the force exerted is: **F = 10 kg × 10 ms⁻² = 100 N**.
 
• The **displacement** (d) of the rice bag is **2 meters** (the height at which the bag is lifted).
 
• Therefore, the work done by the worker is: **W = F × d = 100 N × 2 m = 200 J**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **200 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done**__

 __
 
• In physics, **work** is defined as the amount of energy transferred by a force acting through a distance.
 
• The unit of work is the **joule (J)**, which is equivalent to one newton-meter.
 
 
 
• **Force**__
 __
 
• **Force** is a vector quantity that causes an object to accelerate. It is measured in newtons (N).
 
• One newton is defined as the force required to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity**__
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** (g) on the surface of the Earth is approximately **9.8 ms⁻²**, but it is often rounded to **10 ms⁻²** for simplicity in calculations.
